frames.narration: The user edits one slide in a 40 MB presentation and saves. The desktop app notices the file changed and cuts it into content-defined chunks of roughly 4 MB, using a rolling hash. Almost all chunks are identical to last time.
The app hashes each chunk and asks which of the 11 hashes the server does not have yet.
Only 2 are new: the chunk around the edited slide and the last chunk. The other 9 are already stored, from the previous version.
The laptop uploads two chunks, about 1 MB in all, instead of 40 MB. If the connection broke here, it would resume with whichever chunk is still missing.

Now the commit. The app says 'this is version 8 of slides.pptx, built on version 7, with these 11 chunks'. The shard accepts it only because version 7 is still current, and adds it to the user's change journal as entry 4,812.

messages.label: v8 on top of v7, 11 chunks

frames.narration: The change notifier tells every other device of this user that the journal has reached 4,812.
The phone asks for everything after the entry it last saw, 4,811, and receives the new chunk list for slides.pptx.
The phone already holds 9 of those chunks from the old version, so it downloads only the 2 new ones. The file is now the same on both devices after about a second.
